subject: MedFlow - conditional minimization of debug logs for PoC
messages:
From: Kendra Alvarez <kendra@medflow.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-10T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Request: minimize debug logs during PoC

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick demo today — the latency looked promising. For the short PoC with our clinical team (6 weeks) we need to limit how long transient debug and stacktrace logs are retained. Our internal policy prohibits storage of session-level debug output beyond 14 days unless expressly approved by security.

Can Redwood support:
- TTL of 14 days for debug-level logs associated with the PoC tenant only
- Immediate deletion workflow for ad-hoc forensic snapshots after triage
- Evidence that the TTL change will be scoped to that tenant and will not affect SOC 2 audit trails

I attached a spreadsheet with the specific retention categories we care about. Also copying procurement and legal as they'll need the formal exception paperwork.

Thanks,
Kendra Alvarez\Security & Compliance Program Manager\MedFlow Health

Attachments: medflow-poc-asks.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Kendra Alvarez <kendra@medflow.health>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-11T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimize debug logs during PoC

Kendra —

Really appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short answer: we can accommodate a tenant-scoped debug TTL for PoC, but we need to confirm the implementation and evidence artifacts so you can satisfy your auditors. High-level plan:

1) Scoped TTL: create a tenant-level retention override that sets debug and trace logs to 14 days. This will be a config flag on your tenant and not the global default.
2) Forensics snapshots: provide a documented workflow for manual snapshot retention and deletion (owner, ticketing, timestamps).
3) Audit evidence: deliver a CAIQ slice + a signed retention-exception form that ties the TTL override to the PoC scope and dates.

I copied Priya on this thread to coordinate the exception form and the CAIQ/traceability artifacts. We also usually include Markus for any required changes to logging configuration and Jonas for the retention verification runbook.

Can you confirm the PoC tenant name and the start/end dates? Once we have that we'll create an exception ticket and ship the evidence pack.

Best,
Evelyn Hart\Director, Security & Compliance\Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-exception-form.pdf (stub)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Kendra Alvarez <kendra@medflow.health>
Date: 2028-09-12T10:20:00-04:00
Subject: Action: MedFlow PoC retention exception - config and evidence

Folks —

MedFlow has asked for a tenant-scoped 14-day TTL for debug/trace logs for a 6-week PoC. They explicitly want: tenant-only override, immediate deletion path for snapshots, and artifacts for auditors (CAIQ slice, exception form, runbook).

Requesting the following from infra/config:
- Markus: schedule a short-lived feature flag to apply the retention override to tenant_id MF-POC-2028. Flag should expire automatically on 2028-10-26 and generate an immutable audit entry. Please confirm the mechanism (config+migration vs. tenant-level policy).
- Jonas: prepare a verification runbook that shows how we'll prove the TTL was applied and that it did not affect global audit logs (SOC 2 scopes). Include sample queries and a time-of-change snapshot.

Timeline: aim to have the config and runbook ready for Evelyn to review by 2028-09-14.

Thanks — Priya

Note: attaching the retention-exception-form filled with the PoC dates once Kendra confirms.

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Kendra Alvarez <kendra@medflow.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal+privacy@medflow.health, procurement@medflow.health
Date: 2028-09-13T08:47:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimize debug logs during PoC

Thanks — confirmed. PoC tenant: MF-POC-2028. PoC window: 2028-09-18 through 2028-10-30 (we included a two-day buffer at the end for wrap-up).

A couple of asks from my side:
- Legal wants the exception form signed and a CAIQ extract that specifically calls out logging/retention controls and how the scoped override is auditable.
- Procurement prefers a DocuSign-ready PDF of the signed exception so we can attach it to the SOW.

If you can provide an initial evidence bundle by 2028-09-14 EOD that includes the CAIQ slice (logging), the retention-exception-form (filled), and a short runbook excerpt that shows the query we can run to validate TTLs, that would be ideal.

Regards,
Kendra

Attachments: medflow-poc-asks.xlsx (previous), retention-exception-form.pdf (draft)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Kendra Alvarez <kendra@medflow.health>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Action: MedFlow PoC retention exception - config and evidence

Quick status update and evidence links —

1) Config: tenant policy MF-POC-2028 created and feature-flagged. The override sets debug/trace retention to 14 days and is scoped to tenant metadata only. Flag is scheduled to auto-expire at 2028-10-30T23:59:59Z. An immutable audit record (policy_change_id: pc-78f4) is emitted to the audit stream when the flag is activated.

2) Verification runbook excerpt: included a test query that returns TTL settings and last-modified timestamps. That query was run in a dry-run against a staging copy — results are in the drive link below.

3) Evidence bundle: CAIQ slice focused on logging controls, the signed retention-exception-form (PDF ready for DocuSign), and the verification runbook excerpt. All artifacts uploaded here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/medflow/pocevidence (read-only link).

Evelyn / Priya — please review the CAIQ slice and exception form for wording. Kendra — once legal signs the form we can enable the flag for your tenant and record the activation timestamp.

Best,
Markus Klein\Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-caiq-evidence.zip (stub)
